design_weight_flow.quote: The fan was designed for a weight flow of 33.248 kilograms per second, an overall pressure ratio of 2.40, an adiabatic efficiency of 0.846, and a rotative speed of 16042.8 rpm.

design_pressure_ratio.quote: The fan was designed for a weight flow of 33.248 kilograms per second, an overall pressure ratio of 2.400, an adiabatic efficiency of 0.846, and a rotative speed of 16 042.8 rpm.

design_speed.quote: and a rotative speed of 16 042.8 rpm.

profile_rotor1.quote: In the first-stage rotor, the blading was of multiple circular arc (MCA) cross section across the entire blade span;

profile_rotor2.value: MCA from tip to 44 percent span, DCA over remainder
profile_rotor2.quote: in the second-stage rotor the blading was MCA from the tip to 44 percent of span and double circular arc (DCA) over the remainder of the span.

profile_stators.quote: Both stators had DCA blading over their entire span. (Percent span is measured from the tip.)

mca_max_thickness_location.quote: For the MCA blading the maximum thickness was specified at 50 percent of chord, and the transition point was located where a normal passage shock was predicted to intersect the suction surface.

mca_choke_margin_target.quote: The turning ratios for all MCA blade elements were selected to provide a choke margin of 4 percent. However, because of an error in the choke margin calculation in the computer program, the actual choke margins were about 3/4 of a percent-age point below the values listed in table III.

design_incidence_rotors_ss.quote: The incidence angles were set at 0° to the suction surface for all the rotor-blade elements and -3° with reference to the suction surface for all of the stator elements.

design_incidence_stators_ss.quote: and -3° with reference to the suction surface for all of the stator elements.

deviation_rule.quote: Deviation angle estimates were based on a modified Carter's rule, as discussed in reference 5, and adjusted to reflect the differences noted between the estimated and measured values presented in references 1 and 2.

rotor1_damper_span_location.unit: percent span from outlet rotor tip
rotor1_damper_span_location.quote: The first-stage rotor had part span dampers to reduce blade vibratory stresses. These dampers were located at 42 percent of blade span from the outlet rotor tip.

rotor1_damper_max_thickness.quote: The maximum thickness of the damper was 0.203 centimeter.

rotor1_damper_edge_radii.quote: Leading- and trailing-edge radii were 0.025 centimeter, and the damper axial chord was 1.129 centimeters.

rotor1_damper_axial_chord.quote: and the damper axial chord was 1.129 centimeters.

rotor1_damper_geometry.value: conical meanline in approximate streamline plane; circular-arc surfaces; axially at blade midchord; not in aero design
rotor1_damper_geometry.quote: The damper meanline forms a conical surface, which lies in the approximate plane of a streamline. ... The outboard and inboard surfaces of the damper were circular arcs tangent to the leading- and trailing-edge arcs. The damper was located axially at blade midchord. The aerodynamic design did not account for loss or local blockage due to the damper.

thickness_distribution.value: rotor 1 and both stators linear hub to tip; rotor 2 cubic
thickness_distribution.quote: The blade thickness distribution of the first-stage rotor and the two stators varied linearly from hub to tip. However, the blade thickness distribution of the second-stage rotor followed a cubic relation to provide an acceptable frequency margin

static_tip_clearance_rotor1.quote: The static radial tip clearances for the first- and second-stage rotors were set at 0.114 and 0.127 centimeter, respectively.

static_tip_clearance_rotor2.quote: The static radial tip clearances for the first- and second-stage rotors were set at 0.114 and 0.127 centimeter, respectively.

running_tip_clearance_rotors.quote: With these dimensions, the running clearances were calculated to be 0.025 centimeter at design conditions.

stator_endwall_clearance.quote: Both stator blade rows were shrouded and had endwall clearances of 0.058 centimeter to provide reset capabilities of ±10° from their design values.

energy_split.value: equal between the two rotors; rotor-exit total pressure radially constant
energy_split.quote: The energy input was divided equally between the two rotors. The design radial distribution of the total-pressure profile at each rotor exit was specified as constant.
